location: No breaking step found. The closest thing to a gap is the sentence after (3): "Uniform summability of |e_p| on compact sets gives local uniform convergence to a holomorphic function".
objection:
I checked every claim in the statement and found no error. The details:
(1) ρ(p)≤min{C0,p} and ρ(p²)≤pρ(p) are correct and need no hypotheses on f.
(4)–(5): the formulas for α_p, β_p, δ_p, the sign and size bounds, and α+β+δ=1−p^{-2} are correct. I confirmed the identities symbolically with sympy.
(6): w_p(h) is correct in all three cases v_p(h)=0, 1 and ≥2, so 0<W_f(h)≤1 and D_f converges absolutely for σ>1.
(8)/(9) and (10)–(12): the coefficient expansions are correct, including the cancelled coefficient δ_p−α_p p^{-2}=−ρ(p)/p³+2/p⁴−ρ(p²)/p⁶. All exponents exceed 1 on the stated ranges, and the tail sums follow correctly from (2). (13) gives a bound uniform in t.
(14)–(16): the local series identity is correct (checked with sympy), and so is the justification for multiplying the series. A numerical test with f=t²+1 at s=3 gives D_f≈0.40305018 and ζ·P_f≈0.40305020, which agree up to truncation error.
(18): the identity P_f=ζ(2s+2)H_f holds on Re s>−1/2.
(19)–(21): the Euler–Maclaurin continuation of ζ is correct. It gives ζ(0)=−1/2 and ζ(−1/2)∈[−1/4,−1/6]; the true value is −0.20789.
(22): the derivation of the constant term γ_E is correct.
(25): D_f(0)=ζ(0)/ζ(2) is correct.
(27)–(28): every local factor M_p(−1/2)=(1−1/p)(α+β√p+δp) is positive and the product converges, so H_f(−1/2)>0 and K_f>0.
(31)–(34): the formula for L_p(1) is correct (checked with sympy), and so is the formula for R_f.
(35)–(37): v is multiplicative because ρ is multiplicative by the Chinese remainder theorem, and λρ/r=ζ(2)^{-2}v. The Euler-product identity is justified by monotone convergence.
The proof cites no literature, so the cutoff rule is not an issue. The only unwritten step is a standard one: going from summable deviations to a convergent product via a Cauchy argument with (3) applied to ∏_{N<p≤M}. Filling it in is routine.
other_issues: Cosmetic: after (3), the proof does not show that the partial products converge (that the infinite product exists). It only bounds the tail product. A one-line Cauchy argument, |P_M−P_N| ≤ |P_N|·(exp(Σ_{N<p≤M}|e_p|)−1), would make this explicit. It is trivially fillable.
Cosmetic: (26), (30) and the remark that both poles are genuine go beyond what the statement asks for. They are correct but not needed.
